ctor.rationale: `base(-1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` with `protected override bool HasEnergyCostX => true` (Cascade.cs:10-15) == `energy_cost_x = True` (cards/base.py:84-87) plus `_energy_cost = 0`. The -1 sentinel does NOT carry the unplayable-cost finding here: `CardEnergyCost`'s constructor sets `Canonical = ((!CostsX) ? canonicalCost : 0)` (CardEnergyCost.cs:86), so an X-cost card's base is 0 in C# too -- the sim's 0 is exactly right, and `GetWithModifiers`'s `if (CostsX) return num` short-circuit matches `Card.energy_cost`'s X handling at the play site.

OnPlay.rationale: `int num = ResolveEnergyXValue(); if (IsUpgraded) num++;` (Cascade.cs:19-23) == `num = self.captured_x + (1 if self.upgrade_level > 0 else 0)` (cascade.py:34); `captured_x` is set by the play pipeline as `hooks.modify_x_value(card, self.player.energy)` (combat.py:1443, formerly :547-549 pre-refactor -- same hook, moved), the sim's ResolveEnergyXValue analogue. REVISED 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep re-audit): as of round 13 (R5), `on_play` no longer reimplements `AutoPlayFromDrawPile` inline -- it now calls the shared `CardPileCmd.auto_play_from_draw_pile(hooks, player, num, position='top', force_exhaust=False)` helper (cmds.py:1714), which is a genuine two-phase pull-then-play: phase 1 pulls all `num` cards into a REAL `player.play_pile` (cmds.py:1751-1771, matching CardPileCmd.cs:954's `Add(cardModel, PileType.Play)`, not a local list as the prior audit pass recorded), reshuffling via `player.shuffle_if_necessary()` per pick (:1753, matching ShuffleIfNecessary at CardPileCmd.cs:941/949-952); phase 2 plays them in order via `combat.auto_play_card(card)`, breaking on `player.is_dead` (:1773-1774, matching CardCmd.cs's IsDead break) with `is_over_or_ending` checked once up front (:1749, matching CardPileCmd.cs:933-936). This closes the former deliberate-divergence guard below: the sim now has a real Play-pile parking step, so a listener sweep during the pull sees the same pile membership C# does.

OnUpgrade.maps_to: handled inline as `+ (1 if self.upgrade_level > 0 else 0)` (cascade.py:34)
OnUpgrade.rationale: Cascade.cs declares NO OnUpgrade override -- the upgrade changes no printed number, it adds 1 to the count read from `IsUpgraded` inside OnPlay. The sim mirrors that exactly, including having no `_on_upgrade`.

guards.what: Cascade must not auto-play itself when its own effect triggers a reshuffle
guards.issue: REVISED 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep re-audit): the prior guard described a now-deleted self-removal dance (`cascade.py:38-40,59-61` pulling itself out of `discard_pile` with a `finally` restore) -- that code is GONE. Cascade's own `on_play` (cascade.py:33-52) is a thin wrapper that never touches `discard_pile` at all; the card it's resolving is wherever the framework's `_playing_card` limbo marker parked it (combat.py:1123-1134, formerly :452-454, same mechanism moved), and the pulled cards live in a real `play_pile` (cmds.py:1751-1771) which `CardPileCmd.shuffle` (the sim's Shuffle) does not read from -- matching `CardPileCmd.cs:870-871`'s Draw/Discard-only scope. Same outcome as before (Cascade itself is excluded from its own reshuffle), reached by a cleaner mechanism; no longer a bespoke per-card workaround.

guards.what: the pull loop stops when both piles are empty, and again when an AfterShuffle listener drains the pile
guards.rationale: `cmds.py:1755-1756` breaks when `draw_pile` is empty after `shuffle_if_necessary()`, matching C#'s `AutoPlayFromDrawPile` break on `cardModel == null` after ShuffleIfNecessary (CardPileCmd.cs:949-952).

guards.what: the play loop bails on `player.is_dead`; combat-over is checked once up front
guards.rationale: `cmds.py:1749-1750` checks `is_over_or_ending(hooks) or player.is_dead` before phase 1 begins (matching CardPileCmd.cs:933-936), and `cmds.py:1773-1774` breaks the phase-2 play loop on `player.is_dead` (matching CardCmd.cs's IsDead break in the per-card loop). Both sides stop; the cards already pulled stay out of the draw pile either way.

guards.what: during the PULL phase, each card is moved into a real Play-pile before any of them resolve
guards.issue: REVISED 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep re-audit): this guard used to be `deliberate-divergence` because the sim held the pulled cards in a local list, in no pile at all. As of round 13 (R5) the sim moves them into `player.play_pile` (cmds.py:1770), a real pile a reshuffle excludes, matching C#'s `PileType.Play` (CardPileCmd.cs:954) exactly. No longer a divergence of any kind -- verdict upgraded to faithful.
